what: A timeline in which each lyric chunk (span) is typed one character at a time is bound to scroll (it starts when the section’s top edge is 20% above the bottom of the screen, ends when the section’s center reaches the screen center, follows .6s late, plays once). Each chunk’s per-character length is random between .01~.05s, so characters are typed in a mix of fast and slow, and chunks with a reading (data-reading) type the reading first and switch to the real characters .1s later. When everything is typed, only the consecutive chunks that become the same text as keep stay underlined, and the rest settle into a faded text color over .5s in random order

options.keep: Text to keep after typing finishes (song title) — if it exactly matches the joined run of text it gets .is-kept, otherwise nothing is sunk
options.min: Lower end of per-character length (s), default .01
options.max: Top end of one character length (sec), default .05
options.swap: Seconds until all the phonetic characters are laid down and swapped for the real text, default .1
options.lag: Seconds the motion lags behind the scroll (scrub), default .6
options.data-reading: (child span) reading sound to print first — kana above kanji, jamo if it is a Korean placeholder

use: Lyrics Song Title
note: Mixing a different font per chunk (a random one of four in the original) is up to the user, who adds a font class to the span. Typing tweens the character count and inserts the sliced text without TextPlugin.

from.where: index.html .pickup__body--float (two blocks of lyrics) — the original uses TextPlugin to set the text of each span over a duration = random(.01, .05, .01) × character count, kana stamped first, then set to kanji at delay .1, ScrollTrigger top-=20% bottom → center center scrub .6 once, when done swaps the song title chunk to a and the rest to color #d5cccb stagger amount .5 random .1s
